site.name: larkfit-mobile
site.summary: larkfit-mobile Fictional fitness tracker "Lark" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Workouts / Activity / You - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full larkfit-mobile system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Larkfit mobile app demonstrates a clean visual hierarchy and consistent navigation state management across tabs. However, significant usability issues exist regarding touch target sizes, which fall below standard accessibility guidelines (44px) for critical controls like filters and settings. Additionally, the 'Activity' tab lacks clear affordances for data filtering, and empty states in search results fail to provide user guidance or recovery options.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the 'Lark' mobile fitness tracker fixture, focusing on navigation flow, data visualization clarity, and interaction feedback within the single-page application structure.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will treat the site as a Single Page Application (SPA), navigating between the four primary tabs (Today, Workouts, Activity, You) to uncover hidden content sections. It will validate the functionality of key interactive elements like the 'Play' buttons for workouts and the '+' action button, while specifically checking for layout stability and touch-target accessibility in both desktop and mobile viewports.
assumptions: The application is a client-side SPA where 'pages' are actually dynamic views toggled via JavaScript, not separate HTML files.
The 'Workouts', 'Activity', and 'You' tabs contain distinct content sections that are currently hidden or off-screen.
The '+' button likely triggers a modal or overlay for adding new data (e.g., logging a workout or meal).
The 'Easy 5K' and 'Hip-mobility' play buttons initiate a workout timer or detail view.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (36x38px) identified in prescan vs 44px guideline
State persistence when switching tabs (does data reset?)
Overflow handling in the 'Activity' charts on narrow viewports
Modal/Overlay dismissal mechanics for the '+' button

phases.title: Baseline & Today Tab Validation
phases.objective: Establish baseline metrics and validate the default 'Today' dashboard layout and scrollability.
key_checks: Verify visibility of all rings (Move, Exercise, Stand) and stats.
Scroll down to ensure 'Today's Plan' and 'Streak' sections are fully accessible.
Check for horizontal overflow issues in the streak calendar widget.
exit_criteria: Full vertical scroll of 'Today' tab completed.
No visual clipping of critical stats observed.

phases.title: Navigation & Content Discovery
phases.objective: Systematically visit all bottom-bar tabs to map the full content inventory of the app.
key_checks: Click 'Workouts': Identify list items, filters, or categories.
Click 'Activity': Locate historical graphs/charts and summary data.
Click 'You': Find profile settings, goals, or connected devices.
Verify active state styling updates correctly on the tab bar.
exit_criteria: All 4 tabs visited at least once.
Primary content headings for each section identified.

phases.title: Primary Interaction: Workout Flow
phases.objective: Test the core user journey of starting a workout from the dashboard.
key_checks: Observe transition: Does it open a modal, new view, or timer?

phases.objective: Validate auxiliary controls and input mechanisms.
key_checks: Click '+' button: Identify the resulting UI (Modal/Form).

phases.title: Mobile Viewport & Accessibility Stress Test
phases.objective: Repeat critical checks in mobile viewport to verify responsive behavior and touch targets.
key_checks: Switch to Mobile Viewport (iPhone SE/Pixel dimensions).
Re-verify tap targets for 'Play' buttons and Tabs (check for overlap).
Test scrolling momentum and bounce effects.
Check if status bar notch overlaps any UI elements.
exit_criteria: Touch target warnings re-evaluated in context.

notes: Since this is a fixture, expect some buttons to be non-functional stubs; focus on UI feedback (hover/active states) rather than backend logic.
Pay attention to the 'small_tap_target' warnings from the prescan during Phase 5.

findings.user_goal: Filter workouts by category (e.g., Run, Bike, Strength) on a touch device.
findings.problem: Horizontal filter chips have a height of only 30px, significantly below the recommended 44px minimum for mobile touch targets.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently detected small tap targets for filter chips (e.g., 'Run', 'Bike', 'HIIT') with heights of 30px across both desktop simulation and mobile viewports. This increases the risk of mis-taps, especially for users with larger fingers or motor impairments.
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets cause frustration and error rates to spike on mobile devices, directly impacting the core functionality of browsing and selecting workouts.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding of filter chips to ensure a minimum hit area of 44x44px, even if the visual design remains compact.

findings.user_goal: Understand why no workouts are appearing after applying a filter and search term.
findings.problem: When a search term conflicts with an active filter (e.g., Search: 'run' + Filter: 'Bike'), the list becomes empty without any explanatory message or 'Clear Filters' option.
findings.evidence: In steps 37-42, the agent observed a completely empty workout list area when conflicting constraints were applied. No 'No results found' text or helper UI was visible to explain the state or offer a reset action.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may perceive this as a bug or broken feature rather than a valid empty state. Without feedback, they don't know how to recover (e.g., should they clear the search? Change the filter?).
findings.suggestion: Display a friendly empty state message (e.g., 'No bike workouts match 'run'') and provide a one-tap 'Clear all filters' button.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Workout list container during conflicting filter/search state

findings.user_goal: Change the date range for activity history (e.g., view 'This week' instead of 'Last 30 days').
findings.problem: The date range selector ('Last 30 days') lacks clear visual affordance indicating it is interactive, and clicking it failed to trigger a dropdown or state change in testing.
findings.evidence: Step agentic-49-click showed that clicking the 'Last 30 days' element resulted in no visible change. The element resembles static text more than a button or dropdown toggle, and layout warnings noted a missing accessible label.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may not realize they can change the time frame for their stats, limiting the utility of the Activity dashboard. If it is clickable, the lack of feedback (hover/active state or dropdown) creates confusion.
findings.suggestion: Add a chevron icon (▼) next to the date range text to indicate a dropdown menu, and ensure the click handler opens the selection options immediately.
findings.source_hint: index.html: 'Last 30 days' selector in Activity tab

findings.user_goal: Access account settings or adjust weekly goals using touch input.
findings.problem: Critical secondary actions like the Settings gear icon (38x38px), 'Adjust goals' button (34px height), and 'Sign out' button (43px height) all fall below the 44px accessibility guideline.
findings.evidence: Final observation and steps 31-36 highlighted layout warnings for these specific elements. The 'Sign out' button is particularly risky as it is at the bottom of the scrollable area, often harder to reach precisely.
findings.why_it_matters: Consistently small targets for administrative tasks make account management difficult and frustrating, potentially leading to accidental clicks on adjacent elements.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding around the Settings icon and the vertical height of the 'Adjust goals' and 'Sign out' buttons to meet the 44px minimum standard.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Settings icon, Adjust goals button, Sign out button

findings.user_goal: Initiate a workout from the detail screen.
findings.problem: Clicking 'Start workout' on the workout detail screen did not trigger a visible state transition (e.g., timer start, new screen) during testing, suggesting a lack of immediate feedback or a functional gap.
findings.evidence: Step 13-18 noted that the 'Start workout' action failed to trigger the expected state transition; the UI remained on the static detail screen. Tool feedback confirmed no URL or text change.
findings.why_it_matters: Primary Call-to-Actions (CTAs) must provide immediate confirmation. If the app is loading, a spinner is needed; if it's navigating, the screen should change. Silence implies failure.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the 'Start workout' button triggers a visible transition, such as a loading state, a modal overlay, or navigation to the active workout timer screen.
findings.source_hint: index.html: 'Start workout' button on workout detail view

gaps: 3 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
